newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu slightly down vs dlr in active market.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu slightly down vs dlr in active market.

text.p: Romania's leu currency ended softer near 6,300/400 to the dollar on Wednesday against some 5,700/6,000 in early trading due to leu inflows on a money market plagued with chronic squeezes, traders said.
Banks' screen quotes continued to show a wide range from 5,800/6,000 to 6,900/8,400 to the dollar, little changed from 5,890/50 to 6,900/8,400 during early trading.
Dealers said short-term rates slipped towards 510 percent from some 520 percent as money market pressures eased as some operators offered leu funds.
"I cannot say exactly where those lei came from, but the money market turned more liquid at noon," said one trader.

Most operators said the foreign exchange market remained confused and keen to see the central bank (BNR) moves at Thursday's refinancing auction, when they expected banks to rush to "gulp" the one-week funds on offer.
"This will be a signal for us. If the BNR trickles in more funds then, the dollar has a chance to consolidate near 6,500 level," said one dealer.
Last week, the central bank's offer of 510 billion lei ($81 million) was heavily oversubscribed, pushing the one-week refinancing rate to 426.5 percent from a previous 226 percent.
Traders said leu squeezes might also prevent banks to buy fresh T-bills or extend the rollover ones at Thursday's public subscription, despite their attractive yield.
The Finance Ministry will offer some 643.24 billion lei in 91-day T-bills with an annual yield calculated at the average of the one-week refinancing rate during their life period.
Latest central bank data put interbank volume at $4.36 million on Tuesday, with overall trading at $18.57 million.
-- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264 ($ = 6300 Romanian Lei)
